guides.definition: A template literal uses backticks and evaluates expressions inside dollar-brace placeholders when the string is created.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: A JavaScript expression evaluated inside the template.

examples.title: Embed a calculation
examples.explanation: JavaScript evaluates the expression and inserts 42 into the resulting string.

guides.definition: const declares a block-scoped binding. The referenced value may still be mutable, but the binding itself cannot be assigned again.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The identifier bound by the declaration.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The expression assigned to the binding.

examples.title: Bind an answer
examples.explanation: answer becomes a block-scoped binding whose value is then logged.

guides.definition: Array.prototype.map calls a callback for each array element and returns a new array containing each callback result.

parameters.name: item
parameters.description: The callback parameter for each value.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: The value returned for each item.

examples.title: Square each number
examples.explanation: map leaves the input array unchanged and returns a new array containing the squares.

guides.definition: Array.prototype.filter calls a predicate for each element and returns a shallow copy containing elements whose predicate result is truthy.

parameters.name: item
parameters.description: The predicate parameter for each value.

parameters.name: condition
parameters.description: A truthy expression for values that should be kept.

examples.title: Keep even numbers
examples.explanation: Only numbers whose remainder is zero pass the predicate and appear in the result.

guides.definition: Object destructuring matches property names from an object value and binds them to local variables in one declaration.

parameters.name: object
parameters.description: The object expression supplying the properties.

examples.title: Extract two properties
examples.code:
const { name, role } = { name: "Ada", role: "Programmer" };
console.log(name, role);
examples.explanation: The declaration creates name and role bindings from properties with the same names.

guides.definition: A function declaration binds a named function in its surrounding scope and may return a value to its caller.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The identifier bound to the function.

parameters.name: argument
parameters.description: The parameter accepted by the function.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: The expression returned to the caller.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: A value used to call the function.

examples.title: Define and call double
examples.explanation: The call passes 21 to value; the function returns 42 and console.log displays it.

guides.definition: A class declaration defines a constructor and methods shared through the class prototype. new creates an initialized instance.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The constructor parameter and instance property.

parameters.name: sample
parameters.description: A value passed to the constructor.

examples.title: Create a Task instance
examples.explanation: new calls the constructor, stores the title, and the instance method returns it.

guides.definition: Promise.all returns a promise fulfilled with an array of results when every input fulfills, or rejected when the first input rejects.

parameters.name: promises
parameters.description: An iterable of promises or plain values.

examples.title: Collect two results
examples.explanation: Both promises fulfill, so Promise.all produces the ordered result array [1, 2].

guides.definition: JSON.parse reads one JSON text and returns the corresponding JavaScript value, throwing SyntaxError for invalid input.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: A JavaScript string containing one JSON document.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: A JavaScript string key read from the parsed object.

examples.title: Read a JSON property
examples.explanation: The JSON object becomes a JavaScript object and its status property is logged.

guides.definition: A try statement runs its block and transfers control to catch when the block throws. finally may be added for unconditional cleanup.

examples.title: Handle invalid JSON
examples.explanation: JSON.parse throws SyntaxError, and catch reports the message without terminating the Node.js session.

guides.definition: Array.prototype.reduce invokes a reducer for each element in order. Supplying an initial value makes the accumulator type and empty-array behavior explicit.

parameters.name: accumulator
parameters.description: The reducer parameter holding the current result.

parameters.name: item
parameters.description: The reducer parameter holding the current element.

parameters.name: initial
parameters.description: The accumulator value before the first element.

examples.title: Total numeric values
examples.code:
const total = [10, 20, 12].reduce((sum, number) => sum + number, 0);
console.log(total);
examples.explanation: The reducer starts at zero and adds each number to produce 42.

guides.definition: Array.prototype.find evaluates elements in order and returns the first value whose predicate is truthy, or undefined when no value matches.

examples.title: Find a value above a threshold
examples.explanation: The search stops at 42, the first value greater than 40.

guides.definition: Array.prototype.some short-circuits at the first truthy predicate result and returns false for an empty array.

examples.title: Detect a matching value
examples.explanation: 42 satisfies the condition, so some returns true without testing later values.

guides.definition: Array.prototype.every short-circuits at the first false predicate result and returns true for an empty array.

examples.title: Validate all values
examples.explanation: Every number is positive, so every returns true.

guides.definition: Array.prototype.flatMap behaves like map followed by flat with depth one, while allowing each input item to produce zero, one, or several output values.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: An item or array returned for each source value.

examples.title: Expand every value
examples.explanation: Each input produces two values and flatMap joins them into one array.

guides.definition: Array.prototype.includes uses SameValueZero comparison, so it can find NaN and treats positive and negative zero as equal.

examples.title: Check for a value
examples.explanation: The array contains 42, so includes returns true.

guides.definition: Array.prototype.sort mutates and returns the same array. A numeric comparison function is required for numeric ordering because the default compares string forms.

parameters.name: comparison
parameters.description: A negative, zero, or positive ordering result.

examples.title: Sort numbers ascending
examples.explanation: The numeric comparator orders the values as 3, 12, and 42.

guides.definition: Object.keys excludes inherited, symbol-keyed, and non-enumerable properties. Its ordering follows the language's property-order rules.

parameters.name: object
parameters.description: The object whose keys are returned.

examples.title: List object keys
examples.explanation: The two own enumerable keys are returned as strings.

guides.definition: Object.entries returns each property as a two-item key-value array and excludes inherited, symbol-keyed, and non-enumerable properties.

examples.title: Read key-value pairs
examples.explanation: Destructuring reads the key and value from each returned pair.

guides.definition: Object.fromEntries consumes two-item entries and assigns each key and value to a new ordinary object. Later duplicate keys replace earlier values.

examples.title: Build an object from pairs
examples.explanation: Each pair becomes one own property on the new object.

guides.definition: Object.assign mutates and returns the target. Source properties are processed from left to right, so later sources overwrite the same keys.

examples.title: Merge settings onto a target
examples.explanation: answer is copied onto the existing target object.

guides.definition: Object.hasOwn safely checks own properties even when an object has no prototype or defines a property named hasOwnProperty.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The string or symbol property key.

examples.title: Check an object's own property
examples.explanation: answer exists directly on the object, so the result is true.

guides.definition: Map.prototype.set stores a value under a key using SameValueZero key comparison. Returning the map enables chained set calls.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value stored under the key.

examples.title: Store a keyed value
examples.explanation: set creates the entry and get retrieves its value.

guides.definition: Map.prototype.get retrieves the value associated with a key without changing the map. Use has when undefined could itself be a stored value.

examples.title: Retrieve a keyed value
examples.explanation: get returns the value stored under answer.

guides.definition: Map.prototype.has checks key presence independently of the stored value and does not modify the map.

examples.title: Check key presence
examples.explanation: The map contains the key even if its value is not inspected.

guides.definition: Set.prototype.add inserts a value using SameValueZero equality. Adding an existing value leaves the set unchanged.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: An iterable used to initialize the set.

examples.title: Add one unique value
examples.explanation: 42 is added once and the spread operator exposes the set values as an array.

guides.definition: Set.prototype.has performs a SameValueZero membership test without changing the set.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: An iterable used to initialize the set.

examples.title: Check set membership
examples.explanation: 42 is present, so has returns true.

guides.definition: String.prototype.includes performs a case-sensitive search from an optional starting position and rejects regular expressions.

examples.title: Find a substring
examples.explanation: The exact lowercase substring appears at the end of the string.

guides.definition: String.prototype.split accepts a string or regular-expression separator and an optional result limit. The original string is unchanged.

parameters.name: separator
parameters.description: A string or regular expression identifying boundaries.

examples.title: Split comma-separated text
examples.explanation: Each comma becomes a boundary between returned strings.

guides.definition: String.prototype.replaceAll leaves the source unchanged. A regular-expression search value must use the global flag.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: The string or global regular expression to replace.

examples.title: Replace repeated text
examples.explanation: Both occurrences are replaced in the returned string.

guides.definition: String.prototype.matchAll exposes each match array, capture group, index, and input without mutating the supplied regular expression's lastIndex.

examples.title: Collect every number
examples.explanation: The iterator yields match records for 1 and 22.

guides.definition: Number.isFinite performs no string coercion, unlike the legacy global isFinite function.

examples.title: Validate a finite number
examples.explanation: 42 is finite while positive infinity is not.

guides.definition: Promise.allSettled never rejects because an input rejects. It preserves input order and reports each outcome with a fulfilled or rejected status.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: An iterable of values or promises.

examples.title: Inspect mixed promise outcomes
examples.explanation: The result records one fulfilled and one rejected input without rejecting the outer promise.

guides.definition: Promise.race settles asynchronously with the first fulfillment or rejection. Other operations continue unless separately cancelled.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: An iterable of values or promises.

examples.title: Select the immediate result
examples.explanation: The already-resolved promise wins the race and supplies 42.

guides.definition: parseInt reads valid digits from the beginning of a string and stops at the first invalid character. Supplying the radix avoids ambiguous intent.

examples.title: Parse a hexadecimal value
examples.explanation: 2a in base 16 equals 42 in decimal.

guides.definition: The optional-chaining operator returns undefined instead of throwing when its left operand is nullish. It does not suppress errors from later non-optional operations.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The object expression that may be nullish.

parameters.name: property
parameters.description: The property path followed after the optional operator.

examples.title: Read a missing nested value safely
examples.explanation: Evaluation stops at the null user and returns undefined.

guides.definition: The nullish-coalescing operator preserves valid falsy values such as zero, false, and an empty string, unlike logical OR.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The expression checked for null or undefined.

parameters.name: fallback
parameters.description: The expression evaluated only when the value is nullish.

examples.title: Preserve zero while defaulting null
examples.explanation: Zero is retained, while null selects the fallback.

guides.definition: Spread syntax is context-sensitive: arrays and calls consume iterables, while object literals copy own enumerable properties into a new object.

parameters.name: left
parameters.description: Values placed first in the result.

parameters.name: right
parameters.description: Values placed after the first iterable.

examples.title: Combine two arrays
examples.explanation: Both iterables are expanded into one new array.

guides.definition: for...of uses the iterable protocol and binds each produced value. It differs from for...in, which enumerates property keys.

parameters.name: item
parameters.description: The binding for each yielded value.

examples.title: Iterate array values
examples.explanation: The loop receives each array value in order.

guides.definition: An async function always returns a promise. await resumes the function after fulfillment or throws the rejection reason inside the async function.

parameters.name: promise
parameters.description: The promise or value to await.

examples.title: Await a resolved value
examples.explanation: The async function resumes with the fulfilled value and logs 42.

guides.definition: Calling a generator function returns an iterator without executing the body immediately. Each next call resumes execution through the next yield or return.

examples.title: Yield two values
examples.explanation: Spreading the generator consumes both yielded values.
